####################################################################################################
Purpose of script: This script prepares the data for models, applying further exclusions based on 
spatial and climate data. The output includes three types of data frames:

- Unipathogen: Single vaccination with a single immunogenicity measurement after vaccination.
- Multi-unipathogen: Single vaccination with multiple immunogenicity measurements (e.g., pertussis).
- Multi-multipathogen: Multiple vaccinations and multiple immunogenicity measurements (e.g., MMR).

Functions Used:
- `fun_dgsk_modpat.R`: Function to create data frames for mono/multi-pathogen and mono/multivariate 
models.

Outputs: 
For each unipathogen, multi-unipathogen and multi-multipathogen (46), in the folder 
outputs/modfit 4 files:
- `data_brms_{i}_v_s08.rds` (for photoperiod models)
- `data_brms_{i}_v_s08_kgc_1.rds` (for photoperiod and climate models up to level kgc 1)
- `data_brms_{i}_v_s08_kgc_2.rds` (for photoperiod and climate models up to level kgc 2)
- `data_brms_{i}_v_s08_kgc_3.rds` (for photoperiod and climate models up to level kgc 3)
####################################################################################################

# Load packages, themes, directories, and functions
```{r}
rm(list = ls())
source("00_pck.R")
source("fun_data/fun_dgsk_modpat.R")
```

# Load the list of data frames per pathogen
```{r}
stu_ppat <- readRDS(glue("{dirs$processed}/stu_ppat.rds"))
# No pertussis combined nor polio combined (as pertussis included dtpa and dtpw and polio ipv and opv)
stu_ppat <- stu_ppat[!(names(stu_ppat) %in% c("pertu", "polio"))]

# Check number of studies and participants
distinct(bind_rows(stu_ppat), study) #110
distinct(bind_rows(stu_ppat), pid, study) #58765
```

# Data frames for unipathogen models ===============================================================
Prepare data frames for unipathogen models
Unipathogen: Single vaccination with a unique or multiple immunogenicity measurements

# Choosing values for method, serology name, and doses by maximizing total individuals
```{r}
dat_comb_uni <- list()
# Unipathogen univariate: 
dat_comb_uni$unipat_mono <- lapply(stu_ppat, function(x) {
  # Filter the dataframes to check which combinations have the highest number of individuals
  x %>%
    filter(if_all(starts_with("reg_"), ~ .x >= 0.8)) %>%
    distinct(study, pid, imm_met_s1, imm_sero_s1, doses) %>%
    group_by(imm_met_s1, imm_sero_s1, doses) %>%
    summarise(pid_n = n(), .groups = "drop")
}) %>%
  bind_rows(.id = "pat_dat") %>%
  group_by(pat_dat, imm_sero_s1) %>%
  # Only under primary vaccination
  filter(doses < 4) 

# Check for alternative methods
group_by(dat_comb_uni$unipat_mono, pat_dat, imm_met_s1, imm_sero_s1) %>%
  summarise(sum(pid_n))

# Continue selection
dat_comb_uni$unipat_mono <- dat_comb_uni$unipat_mono %>%
  # Select the combination with the highest number of individuals
  filter(max(pid_n) == pid_n) %>%
  slice_head(n = 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Label doses and split serology names
  mutate(doses = case_when(doses > 1 ~ "l", doses == 1 ~ "1"),
         imm_met_s1 = strsplit(imm_met_s1, "-"),
         imm_sero_s1 = strsplit(imm_sero_s1, "-"))

# Unipathogen multivariate 
# Pathogens with multiple seronames: "pertua" "men" "strep" "ipv" "opv"
dat_comb_uni$unipat_multi <- lapply(stu_ppat, function(x) {
  # Filter the dataframes to check which combinations have the highest number of individuals
  x %>%
    filter(if_all(starts_with("reg_"), ~ .x >= 0.8)) %>%
    distinct(study, pid, imm_met_s1, imm_sero_s1, doses) %>%
    group_by(study, pid, imm_met_s1, doses) %>%
    summarise(imm_sero_s1 = paste(sort(unique(imm_sero_s1)), collapse = "-"), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(imm_met_s1, doses, imm_sero_s1) %>%
    summarise(pid_n = n(), .groups = "drop")
}) %>%
  bind_rows(.id = "pat_dat") %>%
  # Consider only measurement of multiple immunogenicity values  
  filter(str_detect(imm_sero_s1, "-")) %>%
  group_by(pat_dat) %>%
  # Select the combination with the highest number of individuals
  filter(max(pid_n) == pid_n) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Label doses and split serology names
  mutate(doses = case_when(doses > 1 ~ "l", doses == 1 ~ "1"),
         imm_met_s1 = strsplit(imm_met_s1, "-"), 
         imm_sero_s1 = strsplit(imm_sero_s1, "-"))

dat_comb_uni <- bind_rows(dat_comb_uni, .id = "multi") %>%
  mutate(prefx = case_when(multi == "unipat_mono" ~ "", .default = "multi_"))
```

# Multi-pathogen models ============================================================================
Prepare data frames for multipathogen models
Multipathogen: Multiple vaccination with a unique immunogenicity measurement (mmr, mmr-vzv, hib-men, 
pertua, and pertuw)

# Choosing values for method, serology name, and doses by maximizing total individuals
```{r}
# Create data frames for multipathogen models 
stu_mpat <- lapply(list(
  # Make list of the data frames that are contained in the multi data frame
  "multi_mmr" = c("measl", "mumps", "rubel"),
  "multi_mmr-vzv" = c("measl", "mumps", "rubel", "vzv"),
  "multi_hib-men" = c("hib", "men"),
  "multi_dtpa" = c("dipht", "tetan", "pertua"),
  "multi_dtpw" = c("dipht", "tetan", "pertuw")), function(x) {
    lapply(unlist(x), function(pat_i) {
      stu_ppat[[pat_i]] %>%
        filter(
          imm_met_s1 %in% filter(filter(group_by(dat_comb_uni, pat_dat), !(imm_sero_s1 %in% c(
            "anti_pertu_prn", "anti_pertu_fha"))), (
            pat_dat == pat_i & multi == "unipat_mono" & max(pid_n) == pid_n))[,"imm_met_s1"][[1]][[1]],
          imm_sero_s1 %in% filter(filter(group_by(dat_comb_uni, pat_dat), !(imm_sero_s1 %in% c(
            "anti_pertu_prn", "anti_pertu_fha"))), (
            pat_dat == pat_i & multi == "unipat_mono" & max(pid_n) == pid_n))[,"imm_sero_s1"][[1]][[1]]
          )
      }) %>%
        bind_rows() %>%
        # Make sure the vaccinations occured simultaneously 
        group_by(study, pid, doses, across(starts_with("vac_date"))) %>%
        mutate(across(starts_with("vac_name_v"), ~ paste(sort(unique(.x)), collapse = "-"))) %>%
        ungroup() %>%
        mutate(across(starts_with("vac_name_v"), ~ na_if(.x, ""))) %>%
        filter(if_all(starts_with("vac_name_v"), ~ .x == vac_name_v1 | is.na(.x))) %>%
        arrange(study, pid) 
})

# Multipathogen univariate: 
dat_comb_multi <- lapply(stu_mpat, function(x) {
  x %>%
    filter(if_all(starts_with("reg_"), ~ .x >= 0.8)) %>%
    distinct(study, pid, across(starts_with("vac_name_v")), imm_sero_s1, imm_met_s1,  doses) %>%
    group_by(study, pid, across(starts_with("vac_name_v")), doses) %>%
    summarise(imm_sero_s1 = paste(sort(unique(imm_sero_s1)), collapse = "-"), 
              imm_met_s1 = paste(sort(unique(imm_met_s1)), collapse = "-"), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(doses, imm_sero_s1, imm_met_s1, across(starts_with("vac_name_v"))) %>%
    summarise(pid_n = n(), .groups = "drop")
})  %>%
  # Consider only combinations for all seronames
  bind_rows(.id = "pat_dat") %>%
  mutate(pat_l = case_when(
    pat_dat == "multi_mmr" ~ list( c("measl", "mumps", "rubel")),
    pat_dat == "multi_mmr-vzv" ~ list(c("measl", "mumps", "rubel", "vzv")),
    pat_dat == "multi_hib-men" ~ list(c("hib", "men")),
    pat_dat %in% c("multi_dtp", "multi_dtpa", "multi_dtpw") ~ list(c("dipht", "tetan", "pertu")),
    .default = list(NULL))) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  filter(reduce(pat_l, ~ .x & str_detect(imm_sero_s1, .y), .init = TRUE)) %>%
  group_by(pat_dat, doses, imm_sero_s1, imm_met_s1) %>%
  summarise(pid_n = sum(pid_n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(pat_dat) %>%
  # Select the combination with the highest number of individuals
  filter(max(pid_n) == pid_n) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Label doses and split serology names
  mutate(doses = case_when(doses > 1 ~ "l", doses == 1 ~ "1"),
         imm_sero_s1 = strsplit(imm_sero_s1, "-"),
         imm_met_s1 = strsplit(imm_met_s1, "-"),
         multi = "multipat_multi",
         prefx = "") 

dat_comb_multi$imm_sero_s1
```

# List of data frame combinations
```{r}
dat_select <- bind_rows(dat_comb_uni, dat_comb_multi, .id = "multi_pat") %>%
  mutate(sufx = case_when(multi == "unipat_mono" ~ sub(".*_", "", str_remove_all(imm_sero_s1, "anti_|iga")), 
                          .default = ""),
         sufx = case_when(pat_dat == sufx ~ "", .default = sufx)) %>%
  mutate(multi_pat = case_when(multi_pat == 1 ~ FALSE, .default = TRUE)) %>%
  expand_grid(
    kgc = c(NA, "kgc_1", "kgc_2", "kgc_3"),
    thr = 0.8) %>%
  mutate(name_df = glue("data_brms_{prefx}{pat_dat}{sufx}_v{doses}_s{str_remove(thr, '\\\\.')}_{kgc}"),
         name_df = str_remove_all(name_df, "_NA"))
```

# Create data frames according to the combinations
```{r}
pat_df_l <- sapply(dat_select$name_df, function(x) {
  
  pat_dat <- if(dat_select[dat_select$name_df == x, "multi"][[1]] == "multipat_multi") { 
    stu_mpat 
  } else { stu_ppat }
  
  # TEST STREP ONLY ONE VACCINE
  if(str_detect(x, "multi_strep")) { 
    pat_dat[[dat_select[dat_select$name_df == x, "pat_dat"][[1]]]] <- filter(
      pat_dat[[dat_select[dat_select$name_df == x, "pat_dat"][[1]]]], vac_name_v1 == "strep10") 
  }
  
  # Function to create data frame for mono/multi-pathogen and mono/multivariate models.
  fun_dgsk_modpat(
    dat = pat_dat[[dat_select[dat_select$name_df == x, "pat_dat"][[1]]]], 
    method = dat_select[dat_select$name_df == x, "imm_met_s1"][[1]][[1]],
    seroname = dat_select[dat_select$name_df == x, "imm_sero_s1"][[1]][[1]],
    dose = dat_select[dat_select$name_df == x, "doses"][[1]],
    multi_pat = dat_select[dat_select$name_df == x, "multi_pat"][[1]],
    clim = dat_select[dat_select$name_df == x, "kgc"][[1]],
    clim_thr = dat_select[dat_select$name_df == x, "thr"][[1]])
}, simplify = FALSE)

# Check number of studies and participants
distinct(bind_rows(pat_df_l[str_subset(names(pat_df_l), "kgc", negate = TRUE)]), study)
distinct(bind_rows(pat_df_l[str_subset(names(pat_df_l), "kgc", negate = TRUE)]), study, pid)
length(bind_rows(pat_df_l)$study)

setdiff(distinct(bind_rows(stu_ppat), study)$study,
        distinct(bind_rows(pat_df_l[str_subset(names(pat_df_l), "kgc", negate = TRUE)]), study)$study)
```

# Exclusion per photoperiod and climate group ======================================================
```{r}
# Identify groups that ended up with just one observation 
exclude_1obs_df <- sapply(names(pat_df_l), function(i) {
  lapply(c("reg_2", "reg_3", "reg_4", "reg_6", "kgc_1", "kgc_2", "kgc_3"), function(classification) {
    pat_df_l[[i]] %>%
      group_by(!!sym(classification)) %>%
      summarise(count = n()) %>%
      filter(count == 1) %>%
      rename(value = 1) %>%
      mutate(classification = classification) %>%
      select(classification, value, count)}) %>%
    bind_rows()
}, simplify = FALSE) %>%
  bind_rows(.id = "name_df")

# Exclude groups with only one observation based on photoperiod and climate classifications
pat_df_l <- sapply(names(pat_df_l), function(x) {
  # Fetch the corresponding data frame from the list
  data <- pat_df_l[[x]]
  # Fetch rules for the data frame 
  df_rules <- filter(exclude_1obs_df, name_df == x)
  # Apply filtering for each rule in this data frame
  if(nrow(df_rules) > 0) {
    for (i in 1:nrow(df_rules)) {
      classification <- df_rules$classification[i]
      value <- df_rules$value[i]
      # Filter the data frame based on classification and value
      data <- data %>% filter(as.character(!!sym(classification)) != as.character(value))
    }
  }
  return(data)
}, simplify = FALSE)

# Check number of studies and participants
distinct(bind_rows(pat_df_l[str_subset(names(pat_df_l), "kgc", negate = TRUE)]), study)
distinct(bind_rows(pat_df_l[str_subset(names(pat_df_l), "kgc", negate = TRUE)]), study, pid)
length(bind_rows(pat_df_l)$study)

# hav, ipv, polio, tetan, multi_polio, multi_ipv, multi_dtp, multi_dtpa, multi_dtpw
```

# Total participants 
```{r}
lapply(pat_df_l, function(x) c(studies_vl = length(unique(x$study)), 
                               pid_vl = length(unique(x$pid)))) %>%
  bind_rows(.id = "name_df") %>%
  left_join(dat_select, by = join_by(name_df)) %>%
  filter(is.na(kgc)) %>%
  mutate(imm_met_s1 = sapply(imm_met_s1, paste, collapse = ", "),
         imm_sero_s1 = sapply(imm_sero_s1, paste, collapse = ", "))
```

# Save data frames 
```{r}
walk(names(pat_df_l), function(x) {
  pat <- paste0(dat_select[dat_select$name_df == x, "prefx"][[1]], 
                dat_select[dat_select$name_df == x, "pat_dat"][[1]])
  saveRDS(pat_df_l[[x]], glue("{dirs$outputs}/modfit/{x}.rds"))
})
```

# Exploring the data ===============================================================================

```{r}
# Plot week of vaccination histograms
bind_rows(c(pat_df_l[str_detect(names(pat_df_l), "kgc_3")]), .id = "pat") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = week(vac_date_v1))) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 53) + 
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "turbo") +
  facet_wrap(~pat, scales = "free") + 
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# Plot week of vaccination and immunogencity
lapply(pat_df_l[str_detect(names(pat_df_l), "kgc_3")], function(x) {
  pivot_longer(x, cols = starts_with("imm_val_s1"))}) %>%
  bind_rows(.id = "pat") %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = vac_week_v1, y = log(value), color = name)) + 
    geom_point(alpha = 0.2) + 
    theme(legend.position = "none") + 
    facet_wrap(~pat, scales = "free")

# Plot vaccination events 
# Note: The time between 1st vaccination and last vaccination (max 3), upper limit around 1.3 yrs
bind_rows(pat_df_l[str_detect(names(pat_df_l), "kgc_3")], .id = "pat") %>%
  select(pat, study,rct_group, pid, time_v1_v2, time_v2_v3) %>%
  group_by(pat, rct_group) %>%
  mutate(date_mean = mean(time_v1_v2)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("time_v")) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = (value/7), y = reorder(study, date_mean), color = name)) + 
    geom_point(alpha = 0.2, size = 1) + 
    scale_x_continuous("Weeks between doses", breaks = c(0,4,7,13,14,26,52)) + 
    scale_color_viridis_d() +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    facet_wrap(pat~., scales = "free")

# Plot immunogenicity events 
# Note: The time between last vaccination and immunogenicity, upper limit around 16 weeks
bind_rows(pat_df_l[str_detect(names(pat_df_l), "kgc_3")], .id = "pat") %>%
  select(pat,study,rct_group, pid, time_vl_s1) %>%
  group_by(pat,rct_group) %>%
  mutate(date_mean = mean(time_vl_s1)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = (time_vl_s1/7), y = reorder(study, date_mean))) + 
    geom_point(alpha = 0.2, size = 1) + 
    scale_x_continuous("Weeks (relative to last vaccination)", breaks = c(0,4,8,12,16,20)) + 
    scale_color_viridis_d() +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    facet_wrap(pat~., scales = "free")
```

# Checks ===========================================================================================

# How are the missings distributed?
```{r}
lapply(stu_ppat[unique(dat_select[dat_select$multi == "unipat_multi", "pat_dat"][[1]])], function(x) {
visdat::vis_miss(x %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = imm_sero_s1, values_from = c(censored, imm_val_s1, imm_cutoff_s1)) %>%
  select(starts_with("imm_val_s1")))
})

lapply(stu_mpat, function(x) {
visdat::vis_miss(distinct(x, study, pid, censored, imm_sero_s1, imm_met_s1, imm_val_s1, imm_cutoff_s1) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = imm_sero_s1, values_from = c(censored, imm_met_s1, imm_val_s1, imm_cutoff_s1)) %>%
  select(starts_with("imm_val_s1")))
})
```

# Check the climate threshold, currently 0.8
```{r}
dat_select_sens <- bind_rows(dat_comb_uni, dat_comb_multi, .id = "multi_pat") %>%
  mutate(multi_pat = case_when(multi_pat == 1 ~ FALSE, .default = TRUE)) %>%
  expand_grid(
    kgc = c(NA, "kgc_1", "kgc_2", "kgc_3"),
    thr = seq(0, 1, length.out = 11)) %>%
  mutate(name_df = glue("data_brms_{prefx}{pat_dat}_v{doses}_s{str_remove(thr, '\\\\.')}_{kgc}"),
         name_df = str_remove_all(name_df, "_NA"))

pat_df_sens_l <- sapply(dat_select_sens$name_df, function(x) {
  
  pat_dat <- if(dat_select_sens[dat_select_sens$name_df == x, "multi"][[1]] == "multipat_multi") { 
    stu_mpat 
    } else { stu_ppat }
  
  fun_dgsk_modpat(
    dat = pat_dat[[dat_select_sens[dat_select_sens$name_df == x, "pat_dat"][[1]]]], 
    method = dat_select_sens[dat_select_sens$name_df == x, "imm_met_s1"][[1]][[1]],
    seroname = dat_select_sens[dat_select_sens$name_df == x, "imm_sero_s1"][[1]][[1]],
    dose = dat_select_sens[dat_select_sens$name_df == x, "doses"][[1]],
    multi_pat = dat_select_sens[dat_select_sens$name_df == x, "multi_pat"][[1]],
    clim = dat_select_sens[dat_select_sens$name_df == x, "kgc"][[1]],
    clim_thr = dat_select_sens[dat_select_sens$name_df == x, "thr"][[1]]) %>%
    summarise(across(c(study, pid, country, rct_group), ~ n_distinct(.)))
}, simplify = FALSE) 
pat_df_sens_l <- pat_df_sens_l %>%
  bind_rows(.id = "name_df")

pat_df_sens_l %>%
  left_join(dat_select_sens, by = join_by(name_df)) %>%
  mutate(pat = glue("{prefx}{pat_dat}")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = thr, y = country, color = kgc)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~pat, scales = "free") +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "inferno", begin = 0.8, end = 0.5)
```
